vulnerabilities.description: Temporary file created without explicit permission restrictions. writeFileSync(tmpFile, body, 'utf8') uses default permissions which may be world-readable. An attacker with local access could read sensitive GitHub body content before the file is deleted.

Session files stored with world-readable permissions (644). Session context data containing potentially sensitive information is accessible to other local users. File created with writeFileSync without mode parameter.
Memory data stored in plaintext JSON without encryption. All stored data including context, keys, and values are readable in cleartext. No access controls on .claude-flow/data/memory.json file.

Git command execution output (branch name) displayed without sanitization. While using execFileSync prevents injection, malicious branch names could display ANSI codes or control characters that cause terminal hijacking.
Missing validation of routed agent. The route function returns an agent name that may not exist in AGENT_CAPABILITIES. No error handling if the returned agent is not available in the system.
Race condition possible: loadMemory() does not use file locks. Multiple concurrent calls to set/delete could cause data loss or corruption if operations overlap.
Insufficient input validation in session.update(). The key and value parameters are not validated before being stored in session context, allowing arbitrary data injection.

recommendations: Set explicit file permissions on temp files: use fs.writeFileSync with mode 0o600 (owner-only) for sensitive data
Encrypt session context data using crypto module before storing to disk, decrypt on read
Store memory.json with restrictive permissions (mode 0o600) and consider encrypting keys with sensitive values
Sanitize git output: remove ANSI escape sequences and control characters from branch names before display
Add validation in router.js to verify returned agent exists in AGENT_CAPABILITIES map
Implement file locking (using flock or similar) for memory.json access to prevent race conditions
Add input validation in session.update() to restrict context keys to a whitelist of known safe keys
Document that github-safe.js should only be used with trusted callers, as the tmpdir() is world-accessible
Consider using a secure temporary directory or in-memory buffer for sensitive data instead of /tmp
Add file ownership checks to verify session/memory files are only readable by the current user
